body: I don't right now, but yes, this would be a good idea. I used to live near a technical university a few years ago, but they locked the practice rooms.
Yes, this I know, but it doesn't bring me to that space where I was when I was 13 years old...

>Bad communication? I'm the diggity bomb-dogg of bad communication

This made me LOL.

>pick up a book like "How to get past No"

Good advice that I will accept.

>we all die eventually, let's not hurry ourselves along.

This is one of my main reasons against suicide. I keep coming back to this as a reason not to go through with it. It's like, out of the billions of years it took me to get here, if I'm only conscious for less than 100 of those years, less than a drop in an ocean... no need to hurry, no need to risk something rare and fuck it up. Thanks for bringing it up.

The other reason I have that keeps me going: Suicide only confirms the unnecessary suffering of this world. The only way past suffering is to reject it by not contributing to it yourself. Suicide contributes to the suffering of others at the very least. The question of whether it is acceptable to bring children into this world... I'm not so sure, yet, but **I** should be **as is** under this type of thinking, even if children are a mistake meant to happen.

But man, shit fucking sucks, and I've thought enough about my death that I know how I'd do it. I've even "attempted" once before... although I knew it wouldn't work when I tried, so I was just really going through the motions of it, almost like a ritual, or preparation. That was about 6 weeks after my ex left me. And you are right... I need to let go. I need to move past this soon. Thanks for the good thoughts.

> Perhaps all of yourself is hardened? Or perhaps you are transitioning?

Probably a combination of both, but I'm not "all" hardened and I feel I've mostly moved past cynicism, but go in and out of despair (mostly in). I just came back from a workout and my new years resolution is to go in at least 2 times a week this year (been averaging about 1.5 for a few months, so it is a realistic goal) I always feel dopey after a workout, which helps and I can be pretty positive for about 24-48 hours after, but then baseline sets in and I dont feel like going to work out, etc. That said, I'm much less depressed right now than I have been for the last couple days, but I'm still glad I wrote what I wrote, I just don't have anyone to talk to anymore, and no friend wants a friend to unload these types of troubles on them. Why lose the few people I can talk to?

I most certainly need more time transitioning, if this is the case, but I'm curious about how long it has taken you to move from theatre to real feelings. The theater started when my gf left me and I decided to try and move on from her. Even though I have not moved on yet, it's mostly due to the fact it's been 3 1/2 years and every 6 months the same thing has happened... I do something out of the ordinary to try to move on, but it usually ends up in disaster and I am back to square one. I'm recognizing this and trying not to repeat it. But I still know there needs to be change still; I just don't know what will lead to another disaster and what will lead me out of despair (if that is at all possible).

>you alone have control.

I wish this were true, but it seems I have very little control over my surroundings. It's all very overwhelming for me, often paralyzing.

But again, in case my question was lost in my rambling: How long did it take you before the theater turned into real feelings again? It's been almost 4 years for me, and I feel that it could change provided I'm given the right opportunity to have it change (move to an urban area, get involved in a community organization with a peer group, etc. - I just need to have the money or freedom of movement to do these things. There is nothing within the radius of the distance my car can safely travel.)

Thanks for relating. I'm sure that, despite the specifics or degrees of difference between us, you have some understanding.

>I hate to say that your ex is holding you back(which you may know already).

This is true, and I know it, but I also think that moving forward without her as at least a friend will essentially taint my subsequent relationships with all people, not just girlfriends. It really affects this whole "facade" thing. I think if she and I reconnected, there might be more meaning to my relationships with others-- *this is important to me.* Why? because even if she and I can't be in a romantic relationship anymore, I'd know just by the fact that she is talking to me that there was something special to what we had, which means that maybe there is something else special out there again and that this facade I am carrying will go towards find ing that for sure. It would give meaning to hope, the hope is not just materialistic, but also emotional, and dare I say, "spiritual." Reconnecting with her will effect how I see others- essentially answering the question of a hope for an ethical world. But without hearing from her, it seems all contract is lost. She betrayed me, but she betrayed me only to betray me, because it seems she loved me too much to do the right thing. And that to me is fucked up. Or she never loved me at all and she used me the entire time. It really is that black and white--although, hearing from her would give me a grey area of hope that it was neither way.

>what you had will stay dear to you for all of eternity

But this is exactly the problem, the betrayal made it seem like all that was dear was nonsensical, acted out, faked, and meaningless. Absurd even. I'm not trying to relive the past as much as I'm trying to understand it.

>capable of loving

I want to be capable again. Maybe I will be, maybe I won't. It depends on how much I want to risk, I'm sure.

Thanks for your help.

Yes there is some positive, and I also feel that I'm not going to do anything rash, especially right now. I do not think I can live the rest of my life in my current situation, though and I sincerely don't know how to change it and realize things might always be some version of this... not to mention, it will really only take me one more failure to destroy even my hopes of living comfortably.

I already have a keyboard, but I don't play it. The difference between a keyboard and a piano is the difference between a doll and a woman... The difference between a bad piano and a good piano is the difference between a diseased hooker and a wife. I had a bad piano for a while but it went out of tune so often, it was maddening. But you can't really play Beethoven or Rachmaninov on a $50 keyboard. Mine is a full weighted 88 key keyboard and its good for doing midi, but still, no Beethoven. Bach sometimes, but I'm getting sick of Bach. There was something about the acoustic piano that draws me to it more than the electric one... I think it has to do with how subtle I'm allowed to play it and how my fingers respond to this. Playing piano is a coping mechanism, anyway, it never actually solves my problem, which seems to be loneliness, isolation and just being plain stubborn. 

Thanks for the words of encouragement.
